description.narrative:
Stockholm Environment Institutes Asien-kontor (SEI Asien) har på uppdrag av det regionala Sustainable Mekong Research Network (SUMERNET) inkommit med en ansökan till ambassaden för fortsatt stöd i fem år till SUMERNETs nästa fas, kallad SUMERNET 4 All. Programmet kommer under nästa tioårsperiod att fokusera sitt arbete på det strategiska målet "Minska vattenosäkerheten för alla, särskilt fattiga, marginaliserade och socialt utsatta grupper av kvinnor och män i Mekongregionen". För den initiala femårsperioden, från 2018 till 2023, är det ansökta beloppet från Sverige 60 miljoner kronor. Forskningsprogrammet kommer att genomföras i Sydostasien / Mekong-regionen (Myanmar, Thailand, Kambodja, Laos, Vietnam och två provinser i Kina)
Insatsen syftar till att bidra till en hållbar utveckling i Mekongregionen genom att stärka kunskapsbaserade politiska processer och överbrygga avståndet mellan vetenskap och politik. SUMERNET åstadkommer detta genom att välja forskningsfrågor som är direkt relevanta för aktuella politiska debatter, engagera beslutsfattare i alla aspekter av sin verksamhet och bygga kapacitet för hållbar utveckling genom mentorstöd, workshops och annan verksamhet. SUMERNET 4 All kommer att fokusera sina ansträngningar på tre specifika forskningstema inklusive (1) tillgång till vatten, rättigheter och fördelning under vattenbrist, (2) styrning och hantering av översvämningskatastrofer och (3) gränsöverskridande vattensystem. SUMERNET betonar också samarbete, nätverkande och kunskapsdelning, samt samarbete mellan aktörer i olika länder genom projekt och evenemang och syftar därmed till att stärka forskning och politiskt engagemang i hela regionen.
Insatsens totala budget är 60 miljoner kronor. Cirka 28 miljoner kronor kommer att användas till forskningsverksamhet, cirka 15 miljoner kronor till flerpartssamverkan och ca 6 miljoner kronor till kommunikation och dissemination av resultat.

Stockholm Environment Institute’s Asia Centre (SEI Asia) has on behalf of the regional Sustainable Mekong Research Network (SUMERNET) submitted a proposal to the Embassy for continued support for five years to SUMERNET’s next phase, called SUMERNET 4 All. The program will over a ten-year period focus its efforts on the strategic goal “Reducing water insecurities for all in particular for the poor, marginalized and socially vulnerable groups of women and men in the Mekong Region’’. For the initial five-year period, from 2018 to 2023, the amount requested from Sweden is 60 million SEK. The research program will be carried out in South East Asia/Mekong Region (Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and two provinces in China)
The intervention aims to contribute to sustainable development in the Mekong Region by strengthening knowledge-based policy processes and a key aspect of SUMERNET’s work is to bridge science and policy. SUMERNET achieves this by choosing research questions that are directly relevant to current policy debates, engaging decision-makers in all aspects of their activities, and building capacity for sustainable development through mentoring support, workshops and other activities. SUMERNET 4 All will focus its effort on three specific research themes including (1) water access, rights & allocation in times of scarcity, (2) governance and management of flood disaster risks and (3) transboundary interactions with water systems. SUMERNET also emphasises collaboration, networking and knowledge-sharing, connecting partners in different countries through projects and events thereby aiming at continually strengthening research and policy engagement across the region.
The intervention’s total budget is 60 million SEK out of wich approximately 28 MSEK will be used for research activities, approximately 15 MSEK to multistakeholder activities and approximately 6 MESK will be used for communications and outreach.

The SUMERNET 4 All programmes mission is to improve the policies and practices in reducing water insecurity by conducting collaborative research, engaging with the policy process, and promoting scientifically sound research and innovation. Central to its design was integrating gender equality, social inclusion, human rights, conflict sensitivity, environmental integrity, and poverty reduction.
The programmes objectives were to:
Enhance the capacity of knowledge producers (e.g. researchers) to deliver credible, gender-inclusive, human rights-based, conflict-sensitive, and poverty-focused research on key sustainability challenges in the Mekong Region.
Support policymakers and practitioners to develop and implement evidence informed policies, strategies, plans, and programmes that address water insecurity and poverty, guided by the principles of gender equality, social inclusion, human rights, conflict sensitivity, and environmental sustainability.
To improve the understanding of policy influencers (e.g. media, civil society organisations, and think tanks) by providing them with independent, inclusive, and credible knowledge on water insecurity, so they can serve as effective advocates and amplifiers of SUMERNETs research findings in shaping critical policy and practice domains.

Established in 2005, the Sustainable Mekong Research Network (SUMERNET) has been a unique regional platform for researchers across disciplines and countries to work with the decision makers and other stakeholders to inform and influence the policies and practices for sustainable development in the Mekong Region.
The fourth phase, SUMERNET 4 All (20182025), focused on improving the policies and practices in reducing water insecurity for all, particularly for the poor, marginalized, and socially vulnerable groups of women and men in the Mekong Region. SUMERNET has done this by supporting collaborative research, engaging with the policy process, and promoting scientifically sound research and innovation while considering gender and social equality, human rights, conflict sensitivity, environmental integrity, and poverty reduction in the Mekong Region.
Below are some main examples of results achieved and unexpected results achieved stated. In section 1.5, a more extensive collection of achived results are presented in relation to the set goals and objectives to facilitate the analysis.
Achieved Results:
- Over the programme period, SUMERNET 4 All provided funding, mentoring and capacity support to 40 grants that addressed water insecurity across the Mekong countries. This has directly benefited 230 researchers and practitioners, including 101 women (44% of total grantees) and 84 young professionals (37 % of total grantees, 47% women) from five Mekong countries (Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam).
- The multi-country groundwater project, involving researchers from Cambodia, Thailand, and Lao PDR, directly informed the Cambodia National Groundwater Management Framework, launched in June 2025 by the Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology. Research results on aquifer use, monitoring, and local practices were incorporated into the framework, setting sustainable groundwater use guidelines. Government officials acknowledged that the framework could not have advanced at this stage without SUMERNETs scientific evidence and boundary partner engagement.
- SUMERNET supported the development of a Gender Action Plan at An Giang University. This plan, based on SUMERNET-supported gender analysis tools, was formally adopted by the university and is now guiding institutional policies on recruitment, staff training, and student engagement. The process also influenced other universities in Vietnam to consider similar approaches.
Unexpected Results:
All 27 indicators behind expected outcomes were achieved, and out of those 20 indicators exceeded the expected quantitative targets. meaning that 74% of indicator targets exceeded expectations.
- Qualitatively, the progress markers proves an advanced level ("love-to-see") for especially the objective of "supporting policymakers and practitioners to develop and implement evidenceinformed policies, strategies, plans, and programmes that address water insecurity and poverty, guided by the principles of gender equality, social inclusion, human rights, conflict sensitivity, and environmental sustainability". One prominent example is the significant policy impact of a boundary partners flood risk management project in Baan Phai, resulting in a 1.5 million bath allocation from Thai Government for flood risk management implementation - proving linear success of quality research, multistakeholder cooperation and policy action.
- Another one is the creation of the SUMERNET Young professionals (SYP), where initial expectations were to grant young researchers the opportunity to conduct research in their own country context related to the Mekong region and water insecurity. The support and platform SUMERNET provided additionally resulted in the SYP-network to be created with higher ambitions and produced research, created and organized by the SYP members themselves after initial support of SUMERNET.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
